description: Ramirez-Rosa created a formal community-driven zoning process shortly after taking office in 2015, convening neighborhood groups to design public hearings, bilingual notice requirements, and published feedback before he decides whether to support a zoning change.
evidence_quote: Based on the feedback from community meetings, Alderman Ramirez-Rosa decides whether or not he will support a proposed zoning change.
notes: Sources vary on exact start: took office and began a six-month design process in 2015; one secondary source (New America) states 2016; procedures were updated in 2018 to add bilingual signage requirements. Still active as of October 2024 per WTTW coverage of Ramirez-Rosa as 35th Ward alderman.

description: Rodriguez Sanchez's office runs a CDZD process requiring applicants to work with the ward office and partner neighborhood organizations to hold a public hearing before she decides whether to send a letter of support.
evidence_quote: create a clear, consistent, participatory, and transparent zoning process
notes: Rodriguez Sanchez took office May 2019, defeating incumbent Deb Mell; the ward's CDZD guidelines PDF is dated September 30, 2019. Exact process launch date within 2019 not independently confirmed beyond this document date.

description: The 40th Ward office runs a structured process in which developers submit a zoning intake form, hold a public meeting, and receive written community feedback before the alderman issues a written notice of support, opposition, or deferral.
evidence_quote: Direct, community feedback on proposed zoning changes in the ward is a vital component of our process.
notes: Vasquez took office May 2019; the ward website describes the process but does not state the year it was created.

description: Pawar created a resident Zoning Advisory Council of ward residents with land-use expertise to review zoning relief and development requests and advise him before he decided whether to support them.
evidence_quote: Members of ZAC are ward residents selected by the Alderman who have some area of expertise, experience, or interest regarding zoning or development.
notes: Pawar took office May 2011 and is described in secondary sources as having created the ZAC at that time. A contemporaneous document titled 'Pawar Zoning Advisory Committee' was found but not fully verified. Succeeded by Matt Martin in 2019, who continued the ZAC.

description: Martin continued the ward's resident Zoning Advisory Council, which meets monthly to review zoning relief and development requests and make recommendations to the alderman.
evidence_quote: The Zoning Advisory Council meets monthly to review and make recommendations on various zoning relief requests related to development projects.
notes: The ZAC stopped taking new applications shortly after Martin took office on June 7, 2019, indicating continuity of the pre-existing council rather than a newly created one.

description: Osterman's ward office published written guidelines describing a community process for zoning matters, under which the alderman conveys his decision in writing to the relevant city body (Plan Commission, Zoning Board of Appeals, or Committee on Zoning).
notes: The PDF's body text was not machine-readable; only file metadata (created September 2, 2011, author 'Ward48', title 'Development Guidelines_Community_Process[final].doc') and the document's file path were recoverable, so the process content above is inferred from the title and needs manual confirmation. Osterman served 2011-2023.

description: The 48th Ward runs a resident Zoning Advisory Council that reviews development projects and zoning requests and gives feedback to the alderwoman.
evidence_quote: The mission of the ZAC is to provide feedback to the Alderwoman on proposed development projects, zoning change requests, and relevant community engagement.
notes: Manaa-Hoppenworth took office in 2023; the page references a '2023-24 Zoning Advisory Council' cohort, but it is unclear whether the ZAC name/structure is newly created under her or continues Osterman's earlier community process (see prior row).

description: The 25th Ward maintains a resident Zoning Advisory Board intended to give residents a determinative role in the terms of development in the ward.
evidence_quote: the formation of the 25th Ward Zoning Advisory Board is to ensure resident voices are not just heard, but determine the terms upon which a development can take root in our community
notes: Sigcho-Lopez took office in 2019; the board's exact founding year is not stated on the ward website. Page notes over 800 affordable units created/preserved 'since 2019,' loosely suggesting the board dates to around when he took office, but this is not a direct statement.

description: Waguespack's office requires developers to seek input from local community groups before he decides whether to support a zoning change, per published ward guidelines.
evidence_quote: In most cases, particularly those involving zoning changes, Alderman Waguespack will seek input from the local community group(s) before determining whether to move forward with projects.
notes: Waguespack has served since 2007; the guidelines document's founding/adoption year was not confirmed in the fetched content.

description: Cappleman convened a zoning and development advisory committee of ward residents, including neighborhood association leaders, to weigh in on local development proposals.
evidence_quote: was a member of Cappleman's zoning and development advisory committee, which weighs in on local developments
notes: Cappleman served 2011-2023; the committee's founding year was not confirmed.

description: Clay's office runs a community-driven zoning process that contacts block clubs, neighborhood associations, and the Chamber of Commerce for written feedback and posts a two-week online survey before she decides on a proposal.
evidence_quote: Community feedback is central to the decision-making process, which includes contacting the block club, neighborhood association, and Chamber of Commerce in the area where the development is proposed, and requesting written feedback from these groups.
notes: Clay took office in 2023, succeeding Cappleman.

process_name: 2nd Ward public input process for development
description: Hopkins' office facilitates public meetings between developers and community groups on proposed development projects and solicits phone, email, survey, and letter feedback before he takes a final position.
evidence_quote: Alderman Hopkins is committed to a public and transparent process to receive community input regarding proposed development projects in the 2nd Ward.
notes: Hopkins has served since 2015; the founding year of this specific process is not stated on the ward website.

process_name: community input framed through aldermanic discretion
description: As chair of the City Council Zoning Committee, Burnett described valuing community input but explicitly equated 'the people' with the alderman's own judgment rather than describing a formal resident review process.
evidence_quote: I truly believe in community input. I want the people to have a voice. I don't know every nook and cranny of every neighborhood. And when I say the people, I mean the alderman.
notes: Quote is ambiguous between endorsing community input and asserting aldermanic discretion; classified as 'other' rather than states_no_process because Burnett frames it as valuing input rather than disclaiming any process. Burnett resigned from City Council in July 2025.

description: La Spata implemented a public-facing community zoning review process after taking office in 2019, including a monthly 'First Look' public meeting on pending zoning and development matters, later formalized in a written zoning policy dated August 1, 2023.
evidence_quote: The driving values of 1st Ward Community Zoning are transparency, fairness, and equity.
notes: La Spata took office May 2019 succeeding Proco Joe Moreno; the 'First Look' meetings and a public zoning archive date to 2019-2020, while the written zoning policy document is dated August 1, 2023, so the process predates its own formal written policy.

description: Ramirez's office runs a CDZD process in which applicants seek aldermanic support through a public meeting and feedback period, with the office citing resident knowledge of the community as central to zoning decisions.
evidence_quote: Residents' knowledge of the needs and history of our communities is invaluable in the consideration of zoning changes.
notes: Ramirez took office in May 2023 as the first woman to represent the ward; the ward website does not state the exact year the CDZD process was created, so 2023 is inferred from her term start and campaign commitment to create such a process, not stated directly as a founding date.

process_name: unilateral aldermanic zoning control (no documented community process)
description: Federal litigation and press reporting describe Moreno using his sign-off power over zoning and permits to pressure a property owner (Double Door's landlord) into concessions, rather than following any documented community review process; no zoning advisory council or published community process for the 1st Ward under Moreno was found.
evidence_quote: come back to me on your knees
notes: Moreno served as 1st Ward alderman until May 2019, when he was succeeded by Daniel La Spata, who then created a documented community zoning review process (see La Spata row). Absence of a Moreno-era process is based on not finding one, not on an explicit disclaimer statement by Moreno himself, so this is classified as 'other' rather than 'states_no_process'.
